name: Zand and the Historic Core
tagline: Around the Vakil complex, the bazaar and the citadel
description: The old centre along Karim Khan Zand boulevard, holding the Vakil mosque with its twisted columns, the Vakil bazaar and bathhouse, the Arg citadel and the Nasir al-Mulk mosque a short walk south. Everything Shiraz is known for architecturally sits inside this quarter and it is entirely walkable.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the mosques, the bazaar and the citadel on foot
pros: The Vakil complex and Nasir al-Mulk within a short walk
The bazaar for everyday shopping at local prices
All bus and taxi routes converge here
cons: Traffic and noise on the main boulevard
Busy with domestic visitors around the monuments

name: Hafezieh and the Tomb Quarter
tagline: Around the poets' tombs, north of the centre
description: The northern district holding the tombs of Hafez and Saadi, each set in a garden that fills with people reading poetry aloud into the night, which is a genuine and unusual social practice rather than a tourist scene. The area is greener and quieter than the centre and the Quran Gate marks the old road north.
bestFor: Stays that want the gardens and the evening life around the tombs
pros: The tombs of Hafez and Saadi and their gardens
Greener and calmer than the centre
Genuine local evening culture rather than nightlife
cons: Twenty minutes from the bazaar and the mosques
Busy at weekends and during Nowruz

name: Eram and the University District
tagline: Around the botanical garden and Shiraz University
description: The western district holding the Eram Garden, a UNESCO-listed Persian garden attached to the university's botanical collection, and the main university campus. It is the youngest part of the city, with the best chance of finding English speakers, cheaper housing and a student rhythm.
bestFor: Budget stays with the best chance of an English-speaking circle
pros: Eram Garden and the university on the doorstep
The most English spoken anywhere in the city
cons: Twenty minutes from the historic core
Little of the old city here

name: Ghasrodasht
tagline: The garden district west, orchards and villas
description: A western district that was historically Shiraz's orchard belt, with walled gardens, cypress and citrus, now partly built over with villas and apartment blocks but still noticeably greener and cooler than the centre. It is the pleasant residential option and rents reflect that.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting green space and a quieter street
pros: Orchards and gardens rather than dense city
Cooler in summer than the centre
cons: Rents above the average for the city
Fifteen to twenty minutes into the centre
Requires a taxi for most things

name: Marvdasht and Persepolis (55 km northeast)
tagline: The plain below the Achaemenid capital
description: The agricultural town nearest Persepolis, the ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid empire, with Naqsh-e Rustam and its rock-cut royal tombs a few kilometres further. It is an ordinary Iranian working town with almost no tourism infrastructure, used as a base by people who want to be at the site early.
bestFor: A short stay built around Persepolis rather than the city
pros: Persepolis and Naqsh-e Rustam on the doorstep
Very low costs and no tourist pricing
Early access to the site before the coaches
cons: An hour from Shiraz and its services
Almost nothing to do beyond the sites
